statements.text: Just signed the lease for a three-bedroom student flat in Moholt with two flatmates, Mette and Kari.
Started my student researcher position in Professor Dahl's benthic ecology lab today, sorting fjord sediment samples.
Riding to Gløshaugen campus every morning on my mum's vintage blue DBS city bike.
Picked up weekend barista shifts at the Dromedar coffee shop down on Bakklandet to cover rent.
Running my R statistics models on an old ThinkPad T480 running Linux, heavy but reliable.
Bouldering three evenings a week at Grip climbing gym to build up my grip strength.
Doing ten-kilometer Sunday trail runs around Bymarka with my cousin Lars whenever the weather holds.
Kari moved out of our Moholt flat last weekend, so now Mette and I are sharing with Stian.
Decided to go strictly pescatarian this semester, mostly living on salmon, lentils, and sourdough.
Adopted a tiny rescue dwarf hamster named Tove from a student who was moving abroad.
Professor Dahl left for a six-month sabbatical in Tromsø; Dr. Arntsen is supervising my lab project now.
Someone clipped my bike lock outside the library, so I am taking the number 3 bus to campus now.
Started seeing Henrik, a third-year mechanical engineering student who lives over in Singsaker.
My friend Julie got hired as a research assistant in the plankton genetics lab upstairs.
Handed in my notice at Dromedar coffee; starting a front desk job at the Pirbadet pool next Monday.
Tore my meniscus during fieldwork, so no more bouldering or trail running—doing gentle rehab swimming instead.
Bought a massive potted monstera from the plant nursery to sit next to Tove's hamster cage.
Moved out of the Moholt shared flat into my own little studio in Ila overlooking the fjord.
The ThinkPad motherboard fried completely during my data analysis, so I bought an M2 MacBook Air.
The new Ila studio has underfloor heating in the bathroom, which makes Trondheim mornings so much easier.
My doctor told me my ferritin levels are dangerously low, so I stopped being pescatarian and eat meat again.
The therapy pool for my knee rehab at St. Olavs hospital is heated to thirty-four degrees.
Henrik and I broke up on Tuesday; it was mutual but it feels weird being single again.
Seriously looking into applying for an arctic marine biology exchange semester on Svalbard next spring.
Celebrated my 20th birthday on Friday with a fancy dinner at Havfruen restaurant.
Joined the university underwater club on Thursday so I can log dives toward scientific diving certification.
Secured council plot 14 at the Pontcanna community allotments and spent the morning clearing brambles.
Drove my 2011 Volvo V50 estate down to the garden center to load up twenty bags of compost.
Enjoying our brisk three-mile morning walks around Roath Park lake with my neighbor Gareth.
Since retiring from civil engineering, I have agreed to serve as volunteer treasurer for the Cardiff Civic Society.
Attending the fortnightly Tuesday history reading group at Chapter Arts Centre in Canton.
Agreed to foster Bran, a lovely twelve-year-old Welsh terrier whose elderly owner recently passed away.
Keeping a meticulous handwritten notebook of Bran's twice-daily canine insulin injections.
My morning ritual remains two generous mugs of loose-leaf Earl Grey tea with a splash of milk.
Gave up plot 14 and transferred across the allotment path to the larger corner plot 22 at Pontcanna.
Gareth relocated to Swansea last week, so I am now walking Roath Park solo with my trekking poles.
Erected an eight-foot cedar greenhouse on corner plot 22 to start my tomato seeds early.
The Tuesday history group dissolved due to low turnout; I joined the Thursday biography circle at Chapter instead.
Our ancient Baxi gas boiler is playing up again, requiring daily pressure adjustments to heat the radiators.
Parted with the old Volvo estate and purchased a second-hand electric Nissan Leaf for local driving.
Dear Bran passed away peacefully in his basket last night, so the house feels terribly still without him.
My grandson Dylan began his four-year stone masonry apprenticeship over in Newport this week.
Stepped down from the treasurer duties at the Civic Society to take up the quieter position of honorary archivist.
Relying on my trusty Doro clamshell phone for emergency calls whenever I am out in the garden.
On advice from my cardiologist, I have eliminated caffeinated black tea and switched entirely to chamomile brews.
Severe knee arthritis has put an end to park walks; I now do gentle water aerobics at Llanishen leisure centre.
Mulling over the possibility of entering my heritage runner beans in the Cardiff flower show next summer.
The heating engineers finally finished decommissioning the Baxi boiler and commissioned an air-source heat pump.
The hydrotherapy pool sessions at Llanishen are strictly limited to forty-five minutes on Monday and Thursday mornings.
Attended a splendid choral evensong service at Llandaff Cathedral on Sunday afternoon.
My daughter gifted me her spare iPhone SE so we can video call, so the Doro has been retired.
Still spending every dry morning tending plot 22; the greenhouse tomatoes are ripening nicely.
Signed a shared lease on a lovely ceramics workshop on Calle Canelones in Barrio Sur with Camila.
Starting every pottery morning with a strong double cortado made with whole cow's milk.
Throwing all my bowls and vases on a squeaky secondhand manual kick wheel.
Took in a skinny stray ginger cat who wandered into the studio; named him Mateo.
Firing all my bisque ware at the municipal cultural center kilns over in Parque Rodó.
The veterinarian found urinary crystals in Mateo, so I am buying him expensive prescription kidney food.
Started dating Diego, an architect who works at an urban planning studio in Ciudad Vieja.
Dairy has been giving me painful stomach cramps lately, so I switched to oat milk in my morning cortado.
Going to weekly Tuesday evening vinyasa yoga at Espacio Yoga near the rambla to stretch my back.
Managing all my studio invoices and wholesale orders on an ancient thirteen-inch Dell Inspiron laptop.
Camila moved permanently to Barcelona, so I took over the Barrio Sur studio lease entirely on my own.
Splurged on a brand new Shimpo Whisper electric pottery wheel; throwing tall cylinders is effortless now.
Spent Saturday repainting the front entrance door of the Canelones studio a cheerful terracotta orange.
My dermatologists diagnosed contact dermatitis from handling raw terracotta clay, so I have to apply barrier balm.
My younger sister Valentina finally opened her sourdough pastry shop over in Punta Carretas.
Reunited Mateo with his original owner who lived two blocks away, so no more cat food runs.
Joined the cooperative gas reduction kiln at Taller Pocitos, which produces much richer glaze colors.
Cancelled my Tuesday yoga membership and started taking contemporary dance classes on Thursdays at Sala Camacuá.
Diego and I had a long talk and broke up amicably; we want completely different life paths.
Doctor told me coffee is worsening my gastritis, so I gave up cortados for warm yerba mate with herbs.
Allergy patch testing revealed a separate contact allergy to nickel oxides used in my green glazes.
Putting together an application packet hoping to do an autumn wood-firing ceramic residency in Kyoto next year.
The old Dell laptop motherboard completely died yesterday, so I purchased a refurbished fourteen-inch MacBook Pro.
Scored three vintage cast iron cabinet handles at the Tristán Narvaja street fair on Sunday.
Mounted two warm LED spotlight bars directly above the new electric wheel in the workshop.
Started teaching an intimate four-person wheel throwing masterclass on Saturday mornings at my workshop.
Just finished morning milking. 4 cows give a lot of work for one old man.
My eldest, Wanjala, called from Kisumu. He's working at a bank there, very proud.
Got my daughter Nekesa settled at Moi University in Eldoret for her Business degree.
Knee is acting up again. The doctor in town gave me diclofenac, 50mg twice a day.
Bought a new smartphone, a Tecno Spark. Finally I can send photos of the calves.
Rain is hvy. Had to fix the iron sheets on the main shed.
Vet said I should add more calcium to the feed. Maybe I'll do it next month.
Bought two more heifers from my neighbour. Now we are up to 6 cows!
Wanjala's bank transferred him. He packed up and moved down to Mombasa.
My youngest boy, Simiyu, got a job driving a matatu in Kitale.
All three kids came home for Christmas. Missing my late wife, but it was a good day.
Started milking at 4:30 AM now to get the milk to the co-op earlier.
Got a guard dog for the compound. Named him Simba.
Knee pain is worse. Doctor upped the diclofenac to 75mg.
Simba is a good boy. He barks at everything though.
Sold one of the older cows because her yield dropped. Down to 5 now.
I think I will expand the farm next year to plant some maize.
Simiyu bought his own matatu! He is his own boss now in Kitale.
Changed the cooperative I sell to. Brookside pays better.
The vet usually comes on Tuesdays to check the herd.
Correction on that, he comes on Thursdays. My memory is failing!
When I was a boy we used to walk 10 kilometers to school and we had a dog named Bruno.
Nekesa is staying with me for a month while the university is on break.
Dropped my Tecno in the water trough. Had to buy a Samsung A14.
My brother Wekesa got a new Samsung too.
Started giving the cows napier grass from my own plot.
Wanjala hated the heat in Mombasa. He managed to get transferred back to the Kisumu branch.
Woke up at 5:30 AM today. Decided to change the milking schedule to 5:30 permanently, 4:30 was killing me.
Got a second dog, a little terrier mix called Chui to catch rats.
My stomach couldn't handle the 75mg diclofenac. Doctor switched me to ibuprofen 400mg.
The cooperative meetings are now on the first Monday of every month.
Bought a used motorcycle, a Boxer 150, to get around faster.
Nekesa switched her course from Business to Nursing.
Simiyu's matatu broke down and is beyond repair, so he is back to driving for someone else in Kitale.
Had a great dinner of ugali and fish at a local hotel yesterday.
Simba bit a neighbour's sheep. I had to give him away to a farm far from here.
Bought 3 high-yielding Friesian cows! We are at 8 cows now, lot of milk.
Still selling to Brookside, they are very reliable.
Started listening to a farming radio show every evening at 7 PM.
I am allergic to dust, makes my chest tight.
Nekesa moved into a rented room in Eldoret town.
Turns out I also have an allergy to pollen.
The boxer motorcycle was drinking too much fuel. Sold it and bought a bicycle instead.
Oh, sure, I'll just sell all my cows and become a politician.
Doctor said my stomach is better, put me back on the diclofenac but just 50mg again.
Stopped the farming radio show. The new host is boring.
Wanjala got promoted to branch manager at his bank in Kisumu!
Changed my milking schedule back to 4:30 AM. 5:30 was too late for the morning collection truck.
Simiyu got married! Small ceremony in Kitale.
Nekesa graduated! She packed up her rented room and is doing her nursing internship at the hospital in Nakuru now.
Lost two cows to a tick-borne disease. Heartbreaking. Down to 6 cows.
The Brookside collection centre closed. I have to sell to the local vendors now.
My sister came to visit for Christmas. Nice to have family.
Chui caught a huge rat in the feed store today.
Ibuprofen is better for me after all. The diclofenac hurt my stomach again, so back to 400mg Ibuprofen.
Bought a little Nokia push-button phone today. At least the battery on these things lasts forever.
Simiyu and his new wife are expecting a baby in September!
I have started going to the Methodist church on Sundays.
Doctor says I need to watch my sugar, but I love my sweet tea.
I am still selling my milk to the local vendors, they pay cash which is nice.
Living in an upper 2-bedroom duplex on Olive Street in St. James.
Monthly rent on Olive is $1,150, due on the first.
Using a Samsung Galaxy S21 for calls, dispatch messages, and navigation in the cab.
Big Sky Freight assigned me a 2019 Freightliner Cascadia, unit 402, for my long-haul runs.
Big Sky pays me 53 cents a mile on single-driver long-haul freight.
Dr. Patel started me on Lisinopril 10 mg once daily because my blood pressure was creeping up at my medical.
Sarah and I share custody of Toby — alternating weekends plus dinner every Tuesday evening.
Running the Winnipeg to Calgary corridor on Highway 1 as my regular weekly haul.
Joined Shapes Fitness on Pembina Highway so I can lift weights when I'm home in Winnipeg.
My dad Stan is 76, still living alone in his old bungalow in Brandon.
When I was a kid growing up on our farm near Dauphin, dad had a golden retriever named Barnaby who rode everywhere in his pickup.
Started seeing Brenda, an ultrasound tech at Grace Hospital.
Brenda and I usually spend Wednesday evenings together when I'm back off the road.
Toby's minor hockey team practices on Tuesday evenings at 6 at Terry Sawchuk Arena.
My mistake earlier, Toby's hockey practice is actually Wednesday nights at 6 at Terry Sawchuk, not Tuesdays.
Big Sky took back the Cascadia and assigned me a 2022 Kenworth T680, unit 518.
Landlord gave notice that rent on Olive is going up from $1,150 to $1,225 starting April 1st.
Sarah is still driving that blue 2015 Hyundai Elantra she got right before the divorce.
My personal truck at home is a black 2014 Ford F-150 with the 5.0 V8.
Thinking about maybe buying my own rig and becoming an owner-operator once Toby starts high school.
Adopted a 3-year-old German Shepherd mix named Copper from Manitoba Underdogs Rescue to keep me company in the cab.
Toby turns 11 on June 14th, got to make sure I book that weekend off with dispatch.
Blood pressure was still 145 over 92 at my DOT checkup, so Dr. Patel bumped my Lisinopril to 20 mg.
Renting a 10x10 outdoor storage locker at Headingley Storage for my snow tires and extra tools.
The Headingley storage unit is $110 a month on pre-authorized debit.
Subscribed to SiriusXM for the truck radio so I have music and talk through the dead zones.
Cancelled my Shapes membership and joined Anytime Fitness on Regent because they have 24/7 access at truck stops across Canada.
Dispatch shifted me off the Calgary run. Running the cross-border freight corridor from Winnipeg down to Minneapolis and St. Paul now.
Took Toby to the Red River Ex on Saturday, ate way too many mini donuts and went on the Ferris wheel.
Got my cell phone service through Bell MTS on an unlimited Canada-US roaming plan.
Brenda and I split up last week. Totally done, no more Wednesday dinners or weekend plans.
Medical chart has me flagged as severely allergic to penicillin, gives me full-body hives.
Dad sold the Brandon house and moved into an assisted living apartment at Victoria Landing in Portage la Prairie.
Kenworth developed an electrical issue, so dispatch reassigned me to a 2023 Peterbilt 579, unit 614.
Do all my personal banking and chequing with Steinbach Credit Union on Main Street.
Upgraded to a Google Pixel 9 Pro XL yesterday, screen is way clearer for navigation in the cab.
Lisinopril was giving me an annoying dry hacking cough, so Dr. Patel switched me to Ramipril 10 mg.
Sarah and I reworked the custody schedule now that Toby is in grade 5. I take him Thursday after school through Monday morning every other week.
Moved out of Olive Street into a 2-bedroom townhouse on Kimberly Avenue in Elmwood, rent is $1,375 a month.
The Kimberly townhouse has an attached single garage that keeps the snow and ice off the truck overnight.
Diagnosed with mild obstructive sleep apnea at the Misericordia sleep clinic, using a ResMed AirSense 11 CPAP machine in my bunk.
My trucker buddy Gord just took delivery of a custom 2024 Peterbilt 389 glider with dual chrome stacks.
Dr. Patel suggested I take up lane swimming at the Cindy Klassen Recreation Complex to help my lower back.
Sarah traded in her old Elantra and bought a silver 2022 Subaru Forester for driving Toby in the winter.
Annual review with Big Sky: my mileage rate got bumped to 57 cents a mile.
Carl is my fleet dispatcher at Big Sky, guy always makes sure I get home for Toby's long weekends.
Cleared out the Headingley storage unit, hauled my tires and tools to the townhouse garage, and cancelled the $110 rental.
Still driving for Big Sky Freight, still getting steady hauls and zero drama.
Anytime Fitness was always packed with no squat racks free, so I quit and rejoined Shapes Fitness on Pembina again.
Bid on a new lane at work: off the Minneapolis run and back on western Canada, doing the Winnipeg to Edmonton corridor weekly.
Toby talked me into adopting an 8-month-old orange tabby cat named Cheddar from the Winnipeg Humane Society for the townhouse.
Traded in the daily driver and picked up a 2021 Toyota Tundra CrewMax in cement grey.
Got stung by a yellowjacket at a rest area outside Portage and ended up in urgent care, doctor said I'm allergic to wasp stings now on top of penicillin.
Cancelled my SiriusXM subscription, price jumped to $28 a month so I'm strictly podcasts and downloaded Spotify now.
Dispatch assigned me a brand new 2025 Volvo VNL 860 sleeper cab, unit 709, rides like a dream.
Started tying my own flies for walleye and trout during layovers, bought a vise and materials.
Diesel hit two bucks a litre at the Flying J, honestly thinking I should park the truck, buy six sled dogs, and haul freight by dog sled.
Staying at my brother Wayne's house in Regina for four days while Big Sky does scheduled maintenance on my Volvo's DEF system.
My brother Wayne in Regina got promoted to head service technician at Cummins Western Canada.
My blood pressure has been steady at 118 over 76, so Dr. Patel dropped my Ramipril dose from 10 mg down to 5 mg.
Turned 44 today, spent my birthday evening at home with Toby eating Jeanne's Bakery log cake.
Automated a monthly $250 transfer from my chequing account into Toby's RESP mutual fund.
I hate driving Highway 17 north of Superior in December, black ice and blowing snow every single time.
Ported my cell number over to Rogers on a $65 Canada-US 100GB plan because Bell had weak reception along Yellowhead.
Keeping a 24 kg kettlebell in the bunk under the mattress to do swings and goblet squats during my mandatory 30-minute breaks.
just started the night shift at Gen Hosp ICU. exhausting but the pay is better.
my schedule is 5 days on, 2 days off. it's a grind.
renting a bedspace in Malate, it's just a 10 min walk to work.
sent 5,000 pesos to mama and papa in Iloilo today. doing this monthly now.
using an Oppo A9 right now, battery barely lasts the 12hr shift.
taking 5mg melatonin to sleep during the day. the sun is my enemy.
my younger brother Mark just started college at San Agustin back home taking IT.
paying 2,000 a month for a personal loan I took out for my nursing board exams.
the bedspace is too loud during the day, i can't sleep. thinking of moving next year.
got a second-hand Samsung A54 from a friend, finally replacing the dying Oppo.
moved out! got a studio apartment in Sampaloc.
sharing the place with my nursing batchmate, Kim. she brought her cat Muning.
i upped my melatonin to 10mg. still struggling with the daytime noise.
mama said papa's blood pressure is high. worried sick.
valentines on shift. at least i'm dating this guy Paolo, he brought me coffee.
increased my remittance to 8,000 to cover papa's new maintenance meds.
got an air fryer for the apartment. total game changer for quick meals before duty.
Mark shifted his course to nursing! following in his ate's footsteps.
Paolo and I broke up. he couldn't handle my night schedule.
dropped the melatonin entirely. started drinking chamomile tea instead.
my samsung got snatched on the jeepney. using my tita's old nokia keypad for now.
started doing zumba on my days off to stay sane.
bought neon pink rubber shoes specifically for my zumba classes.
Kim got her US visa and moved to Texas! I have the Sampaloc studio all to myself now.
when I was a kid we had a parrot named Coco, he was so loud.
treating myself to an iPhone 13 on installment. no more keypad phone!
Dr. Santos told me to cut back on the 3-in-1 coffee to avoid palpitations.
sending 10,000 to Iloilo now since Mark's tuition went up.
got a promotion! still in the ICU night shift but now I'm senior staff.
commuting from Sampaloc is getting exhausting. looking at condos nearer to the hospital.
signed a lease for a condo in Taft for 15k a month! walking distance to work again.
the Taft condo is so small but the view of Manila Bay is nice.
adopted a stray puspin I found near the hospital, named him Siopao.
Siopao loves the wet food from whiskas.
Mark is thinking of quitting nursing.
duty on christmas eve. eating pancit in the breakroom.
taking a barista course on weekends, just for fun.
Mark officially dropped out and is working at a call center in Iloilo.
my rent for the Taft condo just increased to 18k. outrageous.
back to sending 8,000 for the monthly remittance since Mark is earning his own money now.
allergic to shrimp. discovered it the hard way at a dampa dinner.
also found out I'm allergic to dust mites. this year is great.
Siopao got out and got hit by a car. I'm devastated, he didn't make it.
sure, i'll just quit my job and become a nun.
I couldn't afford the 18k rent anymore, so I moved back into my old apartment building in Sampaloc.
actually my schedule changed. I do 4 days on, 3 days off now.
started dating a med tech named Brian.
Brian is severely allergic to peanuts, so we can't have kare-kare.
finished paying off the board exam loan! that's 2k extra in my pocket.
started doing yoga instead of zumba. better for my back. gave away the pink shoes to my cousin.
Brian and I moved in together. he's staying with me in the Sampaloc apartment.
sorry, I said chamomile earlier - I'm actually drinking peppermint tea before bed.
bought a second-hand Toyota Wigo so I can drive to work instead of commuting.
the wigo eats up so much gas.
staying at Brian's parents house for two weeks while our place is fumigated.
Mark quit the call center and is working as a virtual assistant from home now.
changed my schedule to 3 days on, 4 days off. need the rest.
still at the ICU night shift, still loving the chaos.
Brian and I adopted a golden retriever pup named Milo.
Living peacefully in our ancestral house in Aranmula village with my son Vinod, my daughter-in-law Priya, and my two grandchildren Ashwin and Malavika.
My bedroom is the corner room upstairs on the first floor overlooking the coconut grove; it catches the cool breeze from the river.
Dr. Kurian at Kozhencherry clinic has kept me on Metformin 500 mg twice a day after meals to control my diabetes.
Still keeping our old BSNL landline connection in the hall, telephone number 227845, mainly so elderly relatives can ring us.
Every morning at 6:00 AM I go for my daily walk along the Pampa riverbank pathway to keep my knees from stiffening up.
When I was a little girl in the 1950s, my father kept three native Kasaragod dwarf cows in our family parambu.
The local boy delivers Malayala Manorama to our front veranda every morning by 6:30 AM.
My elder daughter Maya is teaching English literature at the government college in Kozhikode and staying in a rented flat near the beach.
Vinod commutes to his construction work sites across Pathanamthitta on his black Hero Splendor motorbike.
Checking my fasting blood sugar at home every Sunday morning using my Accu-Chek glucometer.
I keep my heavy teakwood prayer table and my large-print Bible beside the window in my first-floor bedroom.
Got reading glasses with a +1.75 power from the local optician in Kozhencherry for reading evening newspapers.
Giving free English grammar tuition to three high school girls from our village on Monday and Thursday evenings from 4:30 to 6:00.
Vinod always fills petrol for his motorcycle at the Bharat Petroleum pump near the junction every Saturday morning.
My neighbor Omana insisted I should drink raw bitter gourd juice every morning for diabetes, but the smell made me sick so I refused to take even a sip.
Heavy monsoon rains have turned the riverbank path into pure mud, so I shifted my morning walk to the paved Aranmula temple ring road at 6:30 AM.
Vinod plucked twenty fresh tender coconuts from our tall palms by the well today; the sweet water was wonderful.
Fasting sugar was high at 168 mg/dL during my clinic visit, so Dr. Kurian increased my Metformin dose to 850 mg twice daily.
With all these smart electric meters they want to fix in the village, I told Priya we might as well light oil lamps like my grandmother did!
Priya keeps a tin of Britannia Marie biscuits on the kitchen counter for me to have two biscuits with my 4:00 PM tea.
Started a new little gardening hobby, hanging purple and white dendrobium orchids in clay pots under our front porch.
Vinod brought home a pair of green lovebirds in a white wire cage for our front veranda; Malu and I feed them millet seeds every morning.
My eyes felt strained, so Priya took me to Titan Eyeplus in Chengannur; doctor tested my eyes and prescribed progressive bifocal spectacles with +2.25 reading power.
Taking Telmisartan 40 mg every morning after breakfast for mild hypertension.
Cancelled the Malayala Manorama delivery and switched our daily morning newspaper to Mathrubhumi because I prefer their literary essays and book reviews.
Went with Vinod to the Aranmula temple for the Valla Sadya feast yesterday; the avial was delicious and I only ate two small spoons of payasam.
My daughter Maya bought a sleek HP laptop in Kozhikode to type up her research articles and lecture slides.
Doctor told me to stop eating flour biscuits, so I swapped the Marie biscuits for a small bowl of dry roasted makhana with my evening tea.
I always have my morning black tea brewed with two crushed cardamom pods and no sugar; Priya makes it just right.
Using an old carved bamboo walking stick that my late brother brought from Wayanad whenever I walk outside the gate.
Blood pressure was 145/92 yesterday, so Dr. Kurian added Amlodipine 5 mg to my morning Telmisartan 40 mg.
Pack of aggressive stray dogs has gathered near the temple junction in the early mornings, so I stopped going there; doing forty brisk rounds inside our walled house parambu at 7:00 AM instead.
Still having my bowl of hot rice kanji with boiled payar and coconut chammanthi every evening at 7:30 PM sharp; light on my stomach.
Finally disconnected our old BSNL landline today; no point paying monthly rental charges when everyone rings my mobile.
Thankamani comes to our house every morning at 8:00 AM to help sweep the courtyard and wash heavy cooking vessels.
Because the twice-daily pills were upsetting my stomach, Dr. Kurian switched my diabetes medication to Metformin 1000 mg sustained release, just one tablet daily after breakfast.
Vinod brought a brochure for rooftop solar panels and thought we should install a 3kW system before summer, but we decided to hold off for now.
Vinod sold his Splendor motorbike and purchased an Ola S1 electric scooter for his site visits and marketing, so we don't need petrol runs to the junction anymore.
Maya received her official government transfer order; she left Kozhikode and has joined Maharaja's College in Ernakulam as Associate Professor.
Maya adopted an indie brown rescue puppy named Appu to keep her company in her Ernakulam apartment.
Dr. Kurian asked me to monitor glucose closer, so I am testing fasting blood sugar every Wednesday and Sunday morning now instead of just once a week.
Staying at Maya's flat in Ernakulam for a week while Vinod gets our ancestral house walls whitewashed and painted before the rains.
Because my knees can no longer manage the staircase, Vinod shifted my bedroom down to the ground-floor guest room next to the dining hall, moving my bed and my wooden prayer table down here.
My new ground-floor bedroom stays very cool in the afternoons because the leafy branches of our old mango tree shade the west window.
Mathrubhumi redesigned their print layout with letters that are far too small and cramped for my elderly eyes, so I cancelled it and switched back to Malayala Manorama.
Priya works as a senior clerk at the Canara Bank branch in Kozhencherry town, taking the private bus every morning at 8:45.
Dr. Kurian noticed mild dryness in my eyes and prescribed Refresh Tears eye drops, two drops in each eye morning and night.
My vocal cords get tired and hoarse after talking continuously, so I have completely stopped taking evening English tuition classes for the neighborhood schoolgirls.
Our grandson Ashwin packed his bags and left for the engineering college hostel in Kalamassery; the dining table feels very quiet without his jokes.
The humid monsoon dampness in the parambu was giving me breathing trouble, so on doctor's advice I now do my thirty minutes of morning walking on our flat concrete terrace upstairs at 6:00 AM.
My monthly teacher's pension gets credited into my savings account at the State Bank of India Kozhencherry branch on the first of every month.
Vinod fitted a sturdy black metal carrying basket on the front of his Ola electric scooter to bring vegetables and milk packets from the bazaar.
My post-lunch blood sugars were creeping up to 210, so Dr. Kurian added Teneligliptin 20 mg once daily before breakfast, alongside my regular Metformin 1000 mg SR tablet.
Cousin Mathew told me to rub eucalyptus oil on my knees for the ache, but the strong smell gives me a headache so I did not use it.
Priya noticed me wobbling on the bamboo stick, so she bought me an aluminum quad cane with four rubber-tipped feet and an adjustable grip that feels far steadier.
We hosted our family pre-Christmas gathering; I cooked my signature Syrian Christian mutton stew and steamed palappams for eighteen guests.
Thankamani moved to Thrissur with her son's family, so we hired Sarojam to come three mornings a week on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday to wash vessels and sweep.
Priya got promoted to assistant manager and transferred from Kozhencherry to the Canara Bank main branch in Chengannur, so she now takes the train or bus from Chengannur.
Malu's 10th standard SSLC state board exams are scheduled to begin on March 10th, so we are keeping the television off in the evenings.
Priya bought an electric air fryer online for making snacks; at this rate they will soon replace all our earthen pots with spaceship gadgets!
I made a mistake about Malu's SSLC exam dates earlier — her school gave the revised government timetable today, and the exams actually begin on March 19th, not March 10th.
Adopted a stray calico kitten that was shivering near our back kitchen steps; Malu named her Meenu and we feed her warm cow's milk and boiled fish.
Checked my blood pressure at the primary health center yesterday and it was 126/80; the Telmisartan and Amlodipine combination keeps it completely steady.
Transferred my pension home branch from SBI Kozhencherry to the new SBI Aranmula junction branch since it is only a five-minute auto ride away.
Priya and Malu helped me repot six of my dendrobium orchids into fresh coconut husk charcoal before the hot summer begins.
Signed up to be a full-time delivery rider for iFood. Out on the streets every single night.
Riding my beat-up Caloi manual bike for the deliveries. My legs are completly dead by the end of the shift.
Living in Grajaú with my mom and my little brother Leo. Commute to the rich areas takes forever.
